Rajat — adding the technical details you requested. Below is a concise annex you can paste into SIG answers; I also attached the CSV isolation matrix that enumerates control mappings (data type -> allowed egress -> logging/retention).

Technical annex (abridged):
- Deployment types: 
  * Dedicated: customer receives a reserved GPU pool. Network connectivity: customer-side VPC peering/VPN with strict route tables; no cross-tenant routing on the host fabric. Optional transit hosts for telemetry live in a separate management VPC.
  * Private (VPC-hosted or on-prem): control plane is customer-managed in their VPC; data plane never traverses Redwood public network except for optional telemetry endpoints over TLS to a customer-approved endpoint.
- Network boundaries: 
  * Host-level namespaces and process-level isolation in the serving runtime; on-host firewall rules default-deny between tenant interfaces.
  * Egress permitted only via explicitly whitelisted outbound rules; egress endpoints are tunable per-customer.
- KV cache and model artifacts: read-only model artifacts are pulled from a private artifact registry using short-lived credentials; model weights are cached locally on GPU hosts and encrypted at rest.
- Audit & telemetry: token-level request logging (anonymized) and request traces are written to the customer tenant's audit bucket when configured; access logs retained per contract.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: routing policy supports model-variant fallbacks to prevent availability loss; falls back to lower-cost model variants within the same isolation boundary.

Attachments included: isolation_matrix.csv (CSV, 45KB) — columns: data_class, allowed_egress, encryption_at_rest, logging_destination, retention_days

If you want a brief diagram showing the Dedicated host fabric with management overlay, I can prepare that as a 1-slide asset. Otherwise Ben/Vanessa already shared the sanitized VPC diagram for your SIG.

—Karthik
